### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/connector-mcp`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/integration.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/integration.json`, `packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_CHANGED (symbol, a top-level const object), computeMcpToolsSnapshot (symbol, a top-level function), toolsSnapshot (symbol, a field of interface McpProviderConfig), CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_CHANGED (literal, a string literal in CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_CHANGED; a string literal in ERROR_CODE_LEDGER), inputSchema (literal, a string literal in mcpToolDigest))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via inputSchema (literal, a string literal in mcpToolDigest))_
- `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`  _(via inputSchema (literal, a string literal in mcpToolDigest))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/integration.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/integration.json`, `packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2f4dd3e69fb57403be0eb72cf505e456eb987369` — the merge of head `e0eb7d604093496a126bca521291d7d2383d4e54` into base `37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2f4dd3e69fb57403be0eb72cf505e456eb987369 && git checkout 2f4dd3e69fb57403be0eb72cf505e456eb987369
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136 e0eb7d604093496a126bca521291d7d2383d4e54 && git checkout -B drift-repro 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136 && git merge --no-ff e0eb7d604093496a126bca521291d7d2383d4e54

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fdacc6798c118adecd31cc6603ebb0ed81612274`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider-errors.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/integration.json, packages/spec/export-origins/integration.json, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/tool-snapshot.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/tool-snapshot.test.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-connector.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin-extension-api.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-upstream-changed.test.ts, content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx, content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx, content/docs/references/api/contract.mdx, content/docs/references/api/error-code-ledger.mdx, .changeset/27401-automation-upstream-changed-degrade.md, .changeset/27401-connector-upstream-changed-marker.md, .changeset/27401-mcp-tools-snapshot.md + packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts on the head, read and not reviewed (`connectorInstanceSignature` :657, the reconcile loop :2402 to :2660, `declarativeRetryDelayMs` and `DECLARATIVE_RETRY_BASE_MS` / `DECLARATIVE_RETRY_MAX_MS` :372 to :382, `failDegradedConnectorInstance` :3112, `scheduleDeclarativeRetry` :4321), packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-credentials.ts (`withoutCredentialThrown` :471 keeps `code` and `status`), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (`registerDegradedConnector` :4084 hands `cause` through), packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts (`providerConfig` :895, an open record), packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-include-credential-scope.test.ts (read for coverage of the credentialed case: no pin in any of its cases)

Inputs, read whole: card #27401 (body; ruling 6506797088, letter B, the per-tool record; ruling 6545635244, letter B, the marker of its own on the same backoff; the dev report 6553367650, treated as claims to verify), PR #28515 (body, the 20-file list, `git diff 99fc050e fdacc679`: 20 files, 961 insertions, 22 deletions, the eight commits from the merge-base including the two merges of `main`), the #28357 contract-review records 6540253498 and 6553099315 (the owed rider's wording), commit d925ac77 (the landed credential path), and the 65 check-runs on this head, read at 2026-11-01T05:13Z: all 65 completed, none failed, none cancelled, none in progress; 57 success (Build & E2E UI, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates and its seven lanes, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test Core and its 8 shards, Test UI and its 16 shards, Type Check UI, TypeScript Type Check and its four lanes, Auto Label, filter); 8 skipped (Lint UI — path-filtered, no `ui/` path in the diff — 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke, Schedule gate, Temporal Conformance, UI Published Artifacts, Dogfood Verify CLI, Dogfood Regression Gate matrix shard). The PR reads `mergeable: true`, `mergeable_state: clean`, head repo = base repo, draft; `main` has not moved any of the touched packages or `connectors.mdx` since the merge-base `99fc050e`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **(1) The spec face.** `CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_CHANGED`, `ConnectorUpstreamChangedError` and `isConnectorUpstreamChanged` have the shape of the three markers beside them: a `readonly code` literal, `cause` assigned by hand (the same compile-target note as the first marker), `name` set, a structural guard that reads `code` and never `instanceof`. The marker's TSDoc is accurate to the materializer on this head: "degrades the instance naming the change (the factory's message) and re-checks it on the same backoff as an outage" is `degradeConnectorInstance` with `fault: 'changed'` on `declarativeRetryDelayMs` (5 s doubling to 5 min, not `held`, so `scheduleDeclarativeRetry` arms it); "an edited pin re-materializes it at once" holds because `connectorInstanceSignature` hashes `providerConfig`, so an edit changes the signature and the reload reconcile re-materializes. The `ConnectorProviderFactory` TSDoc names the two further degrading markers, "each with its own wording and retry policy" — right. The ledger row sits under `@objectstack/spec` in alphabetical place with the `door: 'none'` reading in the row comment, exactly as the `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_REJECTED` row beside it, and the reachability sentence is true (no HTTP door answers with it; the husk's `degradedReason` carries the message, not the code). `api-surface/integration.json` and `export-origins/integration.json` carry the three new names at the right origin; the three `references/api` pages gain the member and the enum count moves 355 to 356. Consistent with the source throughout.
- **(2) The materializer branch.** `isConnectorUpstreamChanged(thrown)` is tested after the credential guard and before the outage guard, calls the same `degradeConnectorInstance` with the same `signature`, `hasLive: existing !== undefined`, `reason` and `cause` as the outage branch, plus `fault: 'changed'`; nothing about it fails boot (no `fail(...)`, the husk is registered, the retry map entry is not `held`). The ERROR wording and the engine WARN clause are the ruling's own words, read off the `cause` the engine already received (`registerDegradedConnector.call(host, def, reason, origin, cause, hold)`), with no signature change; the outage branch's wording is byte-unchanged, and the control test pins it. `withoutCredentialThrown` keeps `code` when it rebuilds a leaking error, so a credentialed instance's drift still reaches this branch. The new test boots the real plugin on `LiteKernel`, pins the ERROR text whole, the WARN clause, the retry at BASE then 2·BASE, and recovery to `ready`; the ablation the report describes (anchor `if (isConnectorUpstreamChanged(thrown)) {` to `if (false && …)`, 3 red / 2 green) is the right split for that file. **`hasLive` on a pin mismatch after an edit** — the report's open question 1 — is consistent with ruling 6545635244 and does not have to change: the ruling binds "the same 5 s to 5 min backoff" and nothing more, the reload contract on `main` says "a changed entry's old connector keeps serving until the new one materializes successfully", the connector that keeps serving is one whose own pin passed at its own materialization, and the exposure a take-down would address (a server that drifted behind a live connector) exists by the card's premise 2 whether or not the entry is edited, so option B would not close it. Taking a live connector down on this marker is a policy change for its own card; recorded under ③.
- **(3) `providerConfig.toolsSnapshot`.** The digest is deterministic and documented in one place: `canonicalJson` sorts object members by key with the default string sort (UTF-16 code units, the JCS order) at every depth, drops `undefined` members, keeps array order, writes primitives as `JSON.stringify` does, no whitespace — for JSON-parsed input that is RFC 8785, as claimed; the pin test hashes two key orders of the same tool equal at depth. What is hashed is `{ name, description, inputSchema }` of the `tools/list` entry as the SDK returns it (the entry is handed to `include` unmodified by `createMcpConnector`, which filters before building anything), so `computeMcpToolsSnapshot` offline and the materializer's check hash the same bytes. Malformed pins (not a plain object, an empty name, a value that is not 64 lowercase hex) throw plain before connecting; a pinned name `include` leaves out throws plain before connecting; both are configuration faults with no marker, as the brief asked. The comparison is ruling letter B: every pinned name looked up on its own, `changed` with the served digest and `missing` reported by name, at most 20 named and the rest counted, a selected-but-unpinned tool left unchecked (a tool the server adds is `include`'s to keep out). **The interaction with the credential path is where this head breaks its own contract** — the must-fix below: the `include` refusal now carves pinned names out of `unknown` regardless of `credentialSent`, so a credentialed instance (http transport, a static `auth` header) whose under-scoped token hides a tool that is both included and pinned no longer takes `ConnectorCredentialRejectedError` (403, both causes, a stored row marked `rejected`, no retry against the same value) but `ConnectorUpstreamChangedError` ("pinned tool … is no longer served … the instance comes back once the server serves the pinned definitions again"), retried on the backoff against the same credential forever and with a prescription that names only the server. The same holds for a pin with no `include`. Pinning every included tool is what the new docs tell the author to do, so this is the recommended configuration, not an edge.
- **(4) The owed rider.** Commit fdacc679 changes two lines of `connector-provider-errors.ts` and nothing else: the last sentence of the `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_REJECTED` TSDoc now reads "an MCP server that lists only the tools the instance's `auth` credential may use, and so leaves out a tool the instance's `include` names, is answered with this marker by the `mcp` provider" — the wording record 6553099315 asked for, on this head. It is the sentence (3) makes false for a pinned tool.
- **(5) `connectors.mdx`.** The key, the digest recipe (three members, absent member left out, nothing else hashed, the JCS rules spelled out, `computeMcpToolsSnapshot` named) and the degraded behaviour (no actions, the reason naming each tool and served digest, `CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_CHANGED` in the logs, the same backoff, recovery, the edit re-materializing) match the code; the fault-table row matches the materializer's ERROR text; the two pre-connect refusals are stated. The page is silent on the overlap the must-fix names: its `include` paragraph (from d925ac77) says a credentialed instance's hidden tool "is degraded as a credential the upstream refuses … names both causes", and the new section says "once pinned, a tool the server stops serving is reported by the pin" — for a pinned, included, hidden tool the two sentences disagree and the code follows the second. **The materializer wording naming `toolsSnapshot`** — the report's open question 2 — keep: it is the ruling's quoted text, the marker's TSDoc and ledger row are provider-neutral, and `fault` on `degradeConnectorInstance` is the seam a second producer's wording would enter through.
- **Accept-set and declarations** — `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` on the PR body match the card; `providerConfig` is an open record in the spec (`z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`), so the new key needs no schema edit and no authorable-surface regen, as `include` before it. The retired spelling `toolsSnapshotSha256` appears nowhere on the head tree.
- **Check-runs as gate verdicts** — read as above; every run completed, none red, cancelled or in progress; Lint UI is path-skipped with no `ui/` path in the diff.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/connector-mcp` minor** (`Metadata-protocol: added`), **`@objectstack/spec` patch** (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: three new exports, nothing an author writes moves), **`@objectstack/service-automation` patch** (`Clause-②: no`, a log wording) — accepted; each changeset carries both declaration lines and the level follows the kind.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Must-fix (FAIL)** — `packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts`: a pinned tool absent from `tools/list` on an instance whose static `auth` reached the server (`credentialSent`) must take the credential path, as d925ac77 routes it and as the `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_REJECTED` TSDoc on this very head states; only a served tool whose digest differs (`drift.changed`, unambiguously the server's) is `CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_CHANGED` there. Shape: under `credentialSent`, do not carve pinned names out of `unknown` (and route a pin-only missing name the same way, both causes named, 403), keep the carve-out as shipped when no credential was sent; add a pin case to `mcp-include-credential-scope.test.ts` or `tool-snapshot.test.ts` with `auth: { type: 'bearer' … }` over http asserting `isConnectorCredentialRejected`, `status` 403 and `!isConnectorUpstreamChanged`; and one sentence each in the docs' pin section and the connector-mcp changeset naming which path a credentialed instance's missing pinned tool takes. Without it the head contradicts its own published TSDoc, reverses the #28311 routing for the configuration the docs recommend, and retries a stored credential against the same value — the loop ruling 6470087293 forbids.
- **Should-fix, wording** — `connector-provider-errors.ts` lines 3 to 28: the file header still says a factory "can fail for two very different reasons" and names only the outage marker; the reason for leaving it (open PR #28357) lapsed when d925ac77 merged. Refresh it to name the four outcomes and three markers; wording only, on this PR or the next touch.
- **Should-fix, wording** — `toolsSnapshotDriftError`: "None of the instance's tools are exposed while a pinned tool differs" is false on the `hasLive` path, where the same ERROR record says "the previously-materialized connector keeps serving" and carries this sentence in its `error` meta. Say what this materialization does ("this materialization exposes no tool") or drop the sentence.
- **`hasLive` policy** — kept as shipped (option A), per ① (2). A take-down of a live connector on `CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_CHANGED` is a separate policy card if the lane wants it; note it would not close the drift-behind-a-live-connector exposure, which needs a periodic re-check (premise 2).
- **Wording names `toolsSnapshot`** — kept as shipped (option A), per ① (5).
- **What the pin does not cover** — `title`, `annotations` and `outputSchema` of a tool are outside the digest by design, as the docs state; matches the card's item text.
- **Skills-docs follow-up** — owed as the PR body says (`skills/**` is Tier H); not this PR's.
- **Serial overlap** — none on the head: `main` has not moved the touched paths since the merge-base, and the head is clean against `main` at the read.

### ④ Design judgment

- **The spec face holds against its ruling and first consumer.** Ruling 6545635244 asked for one marker of its own, a structural guard, a ledger row, one materializer branch with its own wording on the outage's backoff, and `CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` left meaning "unreachable"; each is on the head in the shape of its three siblings and the control test pins the outage's words. The per-tool record (ruling 6506797088) composes with `include` on the same key, is defined over a canonical form an offline tool reproduces, and names the tool. Tried: a key-order rewrite of `inputSchema` (hashes equal, pinned by test); a server that adds a tool (unchecked, kept out by `include`); a pin on an excluded tool (refused before connect); an edit of the pin while degraded (signature changes, re-materializes at once); a credentialed instance whose drift message would carry the token (digests only; `withoutCredentialThrown` keeps `code` regardless). The one case that fails is the credentialed, pinned, hidden tool, where the new branch overrides a landed ruling's route and makes the marker TSDoc this PR itself edits read false — which is why the verdict is FAIL on an otherwise ruled-and-right change.

**Verdict reasoning.** The widening of `@objectstack/spec/integration` is the one the maintainer ruled, shaped like its neighbours, ledgered with the right door, and consistent across source, generated artefacts and docs; the materializer degrades without failing boot on the outage's backoff with the ruled wording; the digest is deterministic and the per-tool comparison is letter B; the owed rider is on the head; every check is green or path-skipped on a head clean against `main`. One interaction is wrong: the pin's carve-out from the `include` refusal ignores `credentialSent`, so the credential path d925ac77 landed and the `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_REJECTED` contract on this head are both contradicted for a pinned tool. A contract sentence false on the head that ships it is a must-fix; FAIL until it is routed and pinned by a test, with the two wording should-fixes free to ride along.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e0eb7d604093496a126bca521291d7d2383d4e54`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider-errors.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/tool-snapshot.test.ts, content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx, .changeset/27401-mcp-tools-snapshot.md + packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/tool-snapshot.ts (`compareToolsSnapshot` :129, `ToolsSnapshotDrift` :114), packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-include-credential-scope.test.ts (the credentialed ctx shape it builds, read for comparison), packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts on the head (the three marker branches :2846 to :2901, read and not reviewed), packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts (`ConnectorBearerAuthSchema` :81, `ResolvedConnectorAuth` :135), the same provider file on `origin/main` (`credentialSent` :469, `sendsInstanceAuth` :539)

Delta review of the one commit `e0eb7d60` ("a credentialed instance's missing pinned tool takes the credential path") over the FAILED head `fdacc679` (record 6553796887, read whole): `git diff fdacc679 e0eb7d60`, 5 files, 166 insertions, 33 deletions. Everything the FAIL record judged and did not name in its ③ is carried as judged; this record re-judges the three items it named against the live code on the new head. Inputs beside the diff: the PR at the read (head `e0eb7d60`, draft, `mergeable: true`, `mergeable_state: clean`, head repo = base repo, 20 files), the merge-base `99fc050e` against `origin/main` (no movement on any touched path since), and the 65 check-runs on this head read at 2026-11-01T05:55Z: all 65 completed, none failed, cancelled or in progress; 57 success (Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates and its lanes, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test Core and its 8 shards, Test UI and its 16 shards, Type Check UI, TypeScript Type Check and its lanes, Auto Label, filter); 8 skipped (Lint UI, path-filtered with no `ui/` path; UI Published Artifacts; Dogfood Verify CLI; the Dogfood matrix shard; Temporal Conformance; 18.x upgrade harness; Schedule gate; Packed-tarball smoke).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Must-fix (the credential path) — FIXED.** Judged point by point against the live code:
  - *The predicate.* `credentialSent` at `mcp-provider.ts` :517 reads `transport.kind === 'http' && sendsInstanceAuth(ctx.auth)` and `sendsInstanceAuth` :673 reads `!auth || auth.type === 'none'` → false, `api-key` with `paramName` → false, else true — byte-identical to `origin/main` :469 and :539, the predicate d925ac77 (#28311) landed. The delta adds no second predicate and no weaker one; the two new uses (:531, :592) read the same `const`.
  - *Included and pinned, missing, credential sent.* :531 now carves pinned names out of `unknown` only when `!credentialSent`, so under a credential the included-and-pinned name falls into `unknown` and takes the existing `include` refusal at :557 unchanged: `ConnectorCredentialRejectedError`, status 403, both causes in the text ("the credential lacks the scopes or permissions these tools need — fix the credential, then set it again — or the declaration names a tool this server does not have — fix providerConfig.include"), connection closed first (:534). That is literally the same statement an unpinned `include` entry executes, not a copy of it.
  - *Pinned, no `include`, missing, credential sent.* `compareToolsSnapshot` puts the name in `drift.missing` (:137); :592 throws `pinnedToolsHiddenError` when `credentialSent && drift.missing.length > 0`: `ConnectorCredentialRejectedError`, 403, both causes worded for the pin ("fix the credential, then set it again — or the server no longer serves these tools — review the change and update providerConfig.toolsSnapshot"), the served list sampled at 20 as the `include` refusal samples it, no token in the text.
